clue.text: Police pictures

definitions.meaning: police officers of the lowest rank, taken collectively
paintings by John Constable, the English landscape artist

explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary officers hold that rank, and the painter John Constable's landscapes are known by his surname in the plural.

clue.text: Having gone astray, no longer studying?

definitions.meaning: having strayed from the intended route
read literally, no longer on a course of study

explanation.definitionFit: A ship drifting from its route has strayed, and a student who has left their programme is literally no longer on it.

clue.text: Latin American music that's saucy

definitions.meaning: a lively dance music from Latin America
in the sense of being a sauce: a spicy Mexican relish

explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' is read not as cheeky but as 'that is a sauce'; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Caribbean-rooted dance music and a spicy tomato relish served as a condiment.

clue.text: Work out a dose with care, providing help with deliveries

indicators.note: to work something out can mean to rework it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to calculate a medicine dose carefully, as if for a midwife assisting at births.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests babies, but telephone dialling prefixes help deliver calls to the right region.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialling prefixes route telephone calls to the right region, so they assist in getting them delivered.

clue.text: Stretchers needed for lots of young boxers, perhaps

definitions.meaning: frames for carrying the sick or injured
broods of puppies; a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.walkthrough: The boxers are dogs, not fighters, though stretchers make the ring seem relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretcher-like beds for carrying patients, and broods of puppies born together, share one word.

clue.text: Woman always nagging son, far from friendly

parts.note: cold means unfriendly

explanation.surface: A mother who keeps nagging her boy has become distant from him.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent nag or shrew, a woman forever finding fault, is a traditional sense of this noun.

clue.text: Rushed to get rent

definitions.meaning: torn apart, past tense of tear

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of 'tear' covers both racing along and ripping something apart.

clue.text: Time non-conformist circle accepted as ideal

indicators.note: the word for the dissenter takes the circle's letter into itself

parts.note: a heretic dissents from accepted doctrine
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A dissenter, once an outsider, has been accepted into a group and now seems an ideal member.
explanation.definitionFit: Something existing in theory or as a concept, rather than in practice, is ideal in the philosophical sense.

clue.text: It helps one fiddle, or otherwise commit offence

indicators.note: read as 'arranged otherwise', the two letters of the little word swap places

parts.note: taken as written
to sin is to commit a moral offence

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person cheat, or else break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests fraud, but it is a violin: the resin is rubbed on the bow. 'otherwise' turns OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists rub this resin on the bow hairs to give them grip on the strings.

clue.text: Rich man's end in fateful disaster

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the following word before the shuffle
a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A wealthy man meets his end in a fateful catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'man's' (ignoring the possessive) is N; put inside FATEFUL and rearranged, it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people are well off, so the adjective is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Port some passed over to the left

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the left means reading backwards
some of the words means just part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A remark about a harbour that some ships sailed past to port.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSEDO runs through 'passed over'; read leftwards it becomes the Black Sea port in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian city on the Black Sea is a major harbour.

clue.text: Type of law that's laid down piece by piece

definitions.meaning: the law of Moses in the Old Testament
describing a picture built from small tiles set one at a time

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Moses names the biblical law, and the noun names tilework assembled fragment by fragment.

clue.text: Bearing not needing replacement often?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' tempts as a machine part that needs replacing, but it is the verb: putting up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerating hardship and lasting a long time are both senses of this participle.

clue.text: Testing occasion for a teacher — or a learner

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run unbroken through 'or a learner' is a coincidence of the charade
L is the learner plate on a British driving pupil's car; the unbroken run through 'or a learner' is a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: Remarks about whether an exam tests the teacher or the pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination is a test that a teacher conducts face to face.

clue.text: Be quick to make appearance with musical instrument

parts.note: looks means appearance
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Advice to arrive promptly carrying one's instrument for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to hurry up and be alert.

clue.text: Cutting in a particular direction, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Cutting in a particular direction, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Cutting in a particular direction, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: said casually, the word sounds like '...', as if telling someone to cut along this part, here, rather than that one

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the word's sound in loose speech, 'dis' for 'this'; the plain meaning is anatomical cutting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a body or specimen apart to study it is the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: In sympathy with partner, confused about work coming up

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the turned-up short work
confused letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A muddled partner is nonetheless sympathetic about the work ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the jumbled partner around the work, which 'coming up' turns upward; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means in harmony or in close accord with someone.

clue.text: Establish direction of art centre that's new within old gallery

indicators.note: the middle pieces go inside the old gallery pieces

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: i.e. stands for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Finding one's way to a new arts centre housed in an old gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery. 'that's' gives IE as in i.e.; 'within' puts the centre pieces inside the old gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or set one's bearings is to establish one's position and direction.

clue.text: Think again about prisoner's identity, your Majesty

parts.note: re means about or concerning
con is a convict, with the 's kept as S
ID is short for identity
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone asks the Queen to look again at a convict's true identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prisoner's' gives CON plus the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To review a decision is to ponder it a second time.

clue.text: Release catch, possibly

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a catch is one way to put a batsman out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, being caught is one way a batsman's innings is ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending someone away and getting a batsman out are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Business at home is making a bit of money

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home-run business turns a small profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal disc of currency is a single small piece of cash.

clue.text: Study ways in which one symphony, initially, is composed

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the following pieces sit inside the streets

parts.note: STS is short for streets
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A music student looks at how a symphony is composed, beginning with the first movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' as streets is the leap; 'in which' puts one and the symphony's first letter inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made up of parts means being formed or composed of them.

clue.text: Sheepish opening for Ode to a Grape?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a vine is the plant on which grapes grow, so it is loosely a grape

explanation.surface: A shy poet starts a poem titled Ode to a Grape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like timid, but it means literally of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or like sheep.

clue.text: Risky business, raising this vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the football pools, a British betting game on match results

explanation.surface: Salvaging a ship is a risky venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a long-running British betting coupon on soccer results.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing boat is a kind of small ship.

clue.text: Easily manipulated individual in factory

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the works

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: An easily led worker in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supple or flexible bends easily, as does a compliant person.

clue.text: Jones collected statement from entrant

definitions.meaning: first name of the English architect ... Jones
what someone going in might say, '...', with its three words run together

explanation.surface: A Mr Jones gathered a witness statement from a new applicant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jones' is the architect and stage designer Inigo Jones; 'collected' means the three words are run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The English architect Inigo Jones is identified by his surname alone.

clue.text: Oilman disorientated in Italian city

indicators.note: a disorientated thing is turned about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused oil executive is lost in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian spelling names the northern city of Milan.

clue.text: Sarcastic abuse of coin liar produced

indicators.note: abuse here means misuse, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A liar's misuse of money produced scornful remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockingly saying the opposite of what is meant is the mark of this archaic adjective.

clue.text: Notice pressure producing ooze

parts.note: to notice is to see
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Applying pressure makes liquid leak out.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that trickles slowly through something leaks out bit by bit.

clue.text: Made an assumption about charged particle in set

indicators.note: the assumption word goes around the particle

parts.note: posited means put forward as an assumption
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: A physicist made an assumption about a charged particle in an experimental set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in a particular spot has been put or set there.
